plan.estimand: Minimum total development sample size for a binary clinical prediction model meeting precision criteria
plan.hypothesis: The fitted prediction model's internal validity meets specified precision targets: maximum absolute difference between apparent and shrinkage-adjusted R-squared (Nagelkerke scale) ≤ 0.05; average predicted outcome risk has margin of error ≤ 0.05

parameters.name: Number of candidate predictor parameters (excluding intercept)
Maximum absolute difference (Nagelkerke R-squared) apparent vs. adjusted
Target average outcome-risk absolute margin of error

assumptions: Binary logistic regression model for prediction development
Shrinkage factor 0.90 applied to calibration slope to derive adjusted R-squared from apparent R-squared
Outcome prevalence 0.174 is the marginal probability in the development sample
pmsampsize 1.1.3 default precision criteria apply: 95% confidence, maximum absolute Nagelkerke R-squared difference ≤ 0.05
No events-per-variable rule invoked; sample size determined solely by precision criteria
Average predicted risk margin of error 0.05 is a secondary precision verification target
Total sample size is the sum of events and non-events
clarification_questions: For the 'average outcome-risk absolute margin of error 0.05': does this target the ±0.05 margin applied to the mean predicted probability, or does it require verification that the margin of error formula used by pmsampsize (based on standard error of the mean predicted risk) yields ≤ 0.05 at the returned sample size?
scientific_notes: Riley et al. (2020) criteria for binary prediction models recommend sample size driven by precision of estimated calibration-in-the-large and overall model performance. pmsampsize implements this via the apparent versus adjusted R-squared difference on the Nagelkerke scale.
The use of shrinkage factor 0.90 reflects anticipated optimism. Adjusted R-squared is computed as (1 - (1 - R_app)^shrinkage) to estimate likely performance in external validation.
Cox-Snell R-squared is appropriate for binary outcomes; pmsampsize converts to Nagelkerke scale internally.
No attrition inflation is applied unless explicitly requested.
Execution will verify that the returned sample size achieves the stated precision targets.
